_description: Colorado SS state-exemption activates at age 65 (CO ssRule = exempt_if_age 65). Single filer with a $60k pension and $30k SS, age 64 → 65 across two years. Year 1 (age 64): SS taxable portion included in CO state base. Year 2 (age 65): SS state-exempt → lower state tax.
_rationale: Single, 2026 → 2027, CO. Pension $60k before-tax + SS $30k = $90k gross. Provisional income = 60000 + 15000 = 75000 → 85% zone → SS taxable = min(0.85·(75000−34000) + 4500, 0.85·30000) = min(39350, 25500) = $25,500. Federal AGI = $60k + $25.5k = $85.5k. Federal taxable = $85.5k − $16.1k std ded = $69.4k → federal tax ≈ $10,408 both years. CO: state base year 1 = $60k pension + $25.5k SS (taxed, age 64) = $85.5k. Year 2 (age 65): SS exempt → state base = $60k. CO std ded $16,100 → state taxable year 1 = $69,400 / year 2 = $43,900. CO 4.4% flat → state tax year 1 ≈ $3,054 / year 2 ≈ $1,932. Δ ordinaryTax (year 2 − year 1) ≈ −$1,122.
name: CO SS Age 65
